source.stem:
Many molecules of J join together in reaction R to form a long chain molecule K.

K is the only product.

Which row describes molecule J, reaction R and molecule K?

options.text: molecule J: polymer; reaction R: addition; molecule K: monomer
molecule J: monomer; reaction R: addition; molecule K: polymer
molecule J: polymer; reaction R: cracking; molecule K: monomer
molecule J: monomer; reaction R: cracking; molecule K: polymer

intelligence.enrichment: To think like a scientist, it is important to ask interesting questions; in the activity, many curious and creative questions can lead to the same given answer. Starting from an answer pushes the learner to imagine a situation that could make the answer sensible, so the quality of the question depends on curiosity and fit rather than one fixed wording. The learner applies the activity rule by inventing a curious, creative question or situation that sensibly leads to the given answer. A school task always has one question and one answer, so the learner should recover the teacher's expected question instead of inventing a curious one.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: The ever-evolving world of science. The student must decide: Decide whether a valid scientific question can be formed from a given answer by inventing a curious situation, instead of only asking the most obvious matching question. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key.
